$comment: Canonical OmniBridge design tokens. This file is the single source of truth
for both platforms and is READ BY TESTS on each side, the same way
protocol/testdata keeps the Rust and Kotlin protocol implementations from
drifting. Change a value here and the platform token tests fail until the
Kotlin and Rust/CSS token tables are updated to match.
Two colour families, and the split matters:
brand.*   the identity hues. Fills, marks, gradients, indicator dots.
on_light.* / on_dark.*  the SAME hues corrected to reach WCAG AA as text
and small icons. Bridge Cyan is 2.40:1 on white; it may never
be used for a text label. See docs/design/BRAND.md.

brand.$comment: The official OmniBridge palette. Cyan -> Blue -> Violet is the sweep; Dark and Surface are the two ends of the neutral ramp.

neutral.$comment: One ramp, anchored at both ends by the brand: 50 is Surface and 900 is Dark. The middle stays genuinely neutral — a tinted grey would put a blue cast on every body paragraph.

on_light.$comment: Brand hues corrected for text/icon use on white or Surface. All >= 4.5:1 on #FFFFFF and on Surface.

on_dark.$comment: Brand hues lifted for text/icon use on the dark surfaces. All >= 6.2:1 on Dark and on surface_elevated.

dark.$comment: Derived from Dark rather than inverted: background sits just below Dark, Dark itself is the card surface, so a card reads as lifted out of the page exactly as it does in light.

status.$comment: Never carried by colour alone: every status pairs this with an icon and a word. See UI-GUIDELINES.md.

brand.$comment: Decorative only — the ribbon, marks, progress fills. Never put text on it: white on Bridge Cyan is 2.40:1.

cta.$comment: The text-bearing gradient, and it is exactly the on_light accent triple. Same three hues as the brand sweep, already corrected, so white clears 5.48:1 at every interpolated point and there is no fourth colour set to keep in step.

progress.$comment: Transfer progress fill. No text sits on it, so the vivid stops are fine.

layout.$comment: The content column. A card stretched to the full width of a tablet is a phone layout that has been pulled, not a tablet layout: past this width the column stops growing and centres. compact_max is the largest width still treated as a phone.

elevation.$comment: Restrained on purpose: the reference leans on 1px borders and a whisper of shadow, not Material's default lift.

motion.$comment: Flow, not decoration. Every duration here is skipped entirely under reduced-motion.

typography.$comment: Inter where the platform can carry it, otherwise the platform's own UI face, which is metrically close. See BRAND.md.

contrast_floor.$comment: Asserted by the token tests on both platforms. Text must clear AA on its own surface.
